title: Household Relief Note: Hardship Waivers Already Granted on the Household's CGM Programs
content:
One household's hardship relief is shared across its Larkfield programs, so a hardship waiver on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program is taken at a household share that reads the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program billing history.

**Note.** The household share is 0.7 when the customer's CGM programs carry hardship waiver adjustments posted within the last 12 calendar months totalling at least 50.00, 0.85 when they carry such adjustments totalling less, and 1 when they carry none; a date falls within the last 12 calendar months when it is later than the same calendar day 12 months earlier.

Before the ceilings and the rounding apply, the waiver — the waivable cost share less the balance adjustments already posted against the named posting — is multiplied by the household share.

The adjustments counted are the balance adjustments with the reason hardship waiver on any of the customer's CGM programs, by their posting dates.

| Hardship waivers on the customer's CGM programs in the last 12 calendar months | Household share |
|---|---|
| totalling 50.00 or more | 0.7 |
| totalling more than 0.00 but less than 50.00 | 0.85 |
| none | 1 |

**Example (hypothetical).** CGM hardship waivers of 35.00 and 15.00 in the last 12 months total 50.00, so the share is 0.7: a waivable cost share of 40.00 becomes 28.00. A single CGM waiver of 49.99 gives 0.85, that is 34.00.
